newsitem.title: USA: Techs cheer US bond breakout, see additional gains.
newsitem.headline: Techs cheer US bond breakout, see additional gains.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury market outlook appears bright after a strong rally on Tuesday broke some technical patterns and painted a bullish scenario going forward, chart analysts said.
"It was a pleasure for technicians this morning," said Walter Burke, senior technical analyst at consulting firm MCM MoneyWacth Inc.
"We were caught in a trading range that was getting narrower and narrower, and volume on the range was getting smaller. Today we broke out of that range," Burke added.

The 6-3/4 percent benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond jumped on Tuesday after the release of a lower-than-expected employment cost index for the third quarter. The indicator rose 0.6 percent against an expected 0.8 percent jump.
The bond was up 1-18/32 at 100-14/32 by midday. Its yield, which had been trapped in a range between 6.80 and 6.86 percent over the last two weeks, dropped to 6.72 percent.
Analysts said charts are suggesting the T-bond yield could slide to as low as 6.68 percent in the current cycle.
If that target is achieved, bonds may then stage a further rally that could bring yields down by another 15 to 20 basis points to around 6.50 percent.

"The market looks more bullish here," said a trader at a primary dealership who trades mostly on technicals. "We did break out of the triangle (pattern) we had been trapped over the last few weeks," he added.
Despite the optimism sorrounding the market on Tuesday, some analysts dropped a word of caution ahead of an upcoming slew of fresh data to be released later this week.

"The market is acting great and it's bullish and happy, but you are still going to have payrolls to be careful about," said Michael Krauss, managing director and chief financial strategist at Chase Securities Inc.

The government will release its October employment report on Friday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. In a Reuters survey, Wall Street economists see non-farm payrolls rising 212,000 in October againsty a 40,000 drop in the previous month. Analysts said, however, that if the market weathers the flood of data this week, a broader, longer-term bullish trend is expected to follow.
They said the U.S. Treasury market could benefit from a possible switch of investors from equities and other fixed-income assets into Treasuries as the economy appears to be slowing down.

"The market does have a technical setup that suggests a risk of a more appreciable upside in Treasuries with money flowing out of stocks, out of corporates, out of high yields and out of mortages into the Treasury market," Krauss said.
Krauss pointed to the poor inflow of money into equity funds last week and a solid technical outlook for the intermediate part of the U.S. Treasury curve as reasons for his longer-term optimism.
"There is a risk that this market starts outperforming if there is more sustained view that the economy is weakening," Krauss said.
